arguments.name: Creeds predate the written Gospels
arguments.conclusion: The earliest Christian creeds were formulated and circulating before the writing of the New Testament Gospels.
arguments.speaker: Gary Habermas
premises: P1: The best-known creeds must be pre-50 AD because 1 Thessalonians, the most commonly dated early book, is usually placed around 48–50 AD.
P2: If Jesus died around 30 AD, the gap between the crucifixion and these creeds is only about 15–20 years.
P3: This places the creeds earlier than Mark and all the Gospels.

st1.quote: That's earlier than Mark earlier than all the gospels.

st2.quote: Because that's the most common date given to 1 Thessalonians.

st3.quote: Some people put 1 Thessalonians at uh 48.

st4.quote: Put this way 33 to 48 is only 15 years.

st5.quote: What are you going to do is make the gap smaller.

st6.quote: That's earlier than Mark earlier than all the gospels.

st8.quote: I often count the creeds well we know for sure that the a number of the best known creeds have to be pre-50.

arguments.prior_art: Gary Habermas, The Historical Jesus (1996) and creeds chapters in his four-volume series

or1.quote: I often talk about the creeds.
or1.why: Restates the standard pre-Pauline-creed dating argument with familiar dating anchors.

or2.quote: Some people put 1 Thessalonians at uh 48.
or2.why: Recycles standard 1 Thessalonians dating rather than new data.

arguments.weakest_link: The pre-50 dating of 1 Thessalonians is asserted from 'most common date' without citation or range of alternatives.
arguments.develop_next: Cite the specific scholars and date ranges for 1 Thessalonians to make the pre-50 anchor testable.

arguments.name: Paul assumes audience knowledge of creedal content
arguments.conclusion: Paul's letters presuppose that his audiences already knew the core creedal definitions about Jesus.
arguments.speaker: Gary Habermas
premises: P1: When Paul writes 1 Thessalonians, he does not define who Christ is or explain what makes him deity.
P2: He assumes his audience already knows those definitions.
P3: In a Greek culture, using 'Lord' without definition would be ambiguous unless the meaning was already established.
P4: This presupposes earlier material that predates 1 Thessalonians.

st1.quote: So that presumes a previous material before first Cor- first Thess.

st2.quote: He he they his audience knows what those definitions are.

st3.quote: And to a Greek culture it'd be really iffy to say Lord in Greek and assume they have the same view of Lord as you do.

st5.quote: Oh, you could say that's only first Thessalonians.

st6.quote: So that presumes a previous material before first Cor- first Thess.

st8.quote: You're talking about the gods and the goddesses of from Rome all the way over to Mesopotamia?

arguments.prior_art: Gary Habermas, pre-Pauline creed tradition arguments (e.g., The Historical Jesus, 1996)

or1.quote: He he they his audience knows what those definitions are.
or1.why: Variant on the standard argument from creedal presupposition.

or2.quote: And to a Greek culture it'd be really iffy to say Lord in Greek and assume they have the same view of Lord as you do.
or2.why: Adds the Greco-Roman 'Lord' ambiguity point as support.

or3.quote: You're talking about the gods and the goddesses of from Rome all the way over to Mesopotamia?
or3.why: Bridges into comparative Greco-Roman religious context.

arguments.weakest_link: The inference from Paul's silence about definitions to a pre-existing creed is an argument from silence.
arguments.develop_next: Show a specific 1 Thessalonians passage where undefined 'Lord' language would be unintelligible without prior teaching.

arguments.name: Other early epistles contain early creeds
arguments.conclusion: Creeds are also found in other early Pauline letters, reinforcing an early date for the oral tradition.
arguments.speaker: Gary Habermas
premises: P1: 1 Corinthians is often dated to around 53 AD and contains creedal material in 1 Corinthians 15:3 and following.
P2: Romans contains major creeds such as Romans 10:9 and Romans 1:3–4.
P3: These letters are early, so the creeds they cite must be earlier still.

st1.quote: Well, they've got to be before those books are written.

st2.quote: Rome Romans has some of the major ones.

st6.quote: So, I don't know if that if that

st8.quote: Corinthians has come back for a lot of people to 53 AD.

arguments.prior_art: Gary Habermas, creedal tradition catalogue in his four-volume series

or1.quote: Rome Romans has some of the major ones.
or1.why: Variant listing of the same creedal texts.

or2.why: Adds Romans 1:3–4 to the standard 1 Cor 15 catalogue.

arguments.weakest_link: The inference that a cited creed must predate the letter containing it needs argument against Paul composing it himself.
arguments.develop_next: Give the linguistic criteria (formulaic style, non-Pauline vocabulary) that mark these as quoted tradition.

arguments.name: Bart Ehrman has dated 1 Corinthians 15 creed to the 30s
arguments.conclusion: Even Bart Ehrman has classified the 1 Corinthians 15 creed as originating in the 30s AD, despite later distancing himself from that view.
arguments.speaker: Gary Habermas
premises: P1: Ehrman previously put the 1 Corinthians 15 creed in the 30s.
P2: Ehrman later said he did not mean that.
P3: Habermas has found 8–10 instances in Ehrman's writings where he says '30s,' and two or three where he says 'first two or three years.'

st1.quote: he was classified putting it in the 30s for the first Corinthians 15 for example and then he's come out and said, "No, he didn't mean that."

st2.quote: I already found a list of I think it's up 10-ish, eight to 10 times where he says 30s and two or three of those he says first two or three years.

st4.quote: But >> I never said that, but it's in his writings.

st5.quote: But >> I never said that, but it's in his writings.

st6.quote: I have already I already found a list of I think it's up 10-ish, eight to 10 times where he says 30s

arguments.prior_art: Bart Ehrman, Did Jesus Exist? / Forged (2011–2012) and his 1 Cor 15 dating remarks

or1.quote: he was classified putting it in the 30s
or1.why: Variant use of Ehrman's concession as a hostile-witness datum.

or2.quote: eight to 10 times where he says 30s and two or three of those he says first two or three years
or2.why: Brings a textual tally of Ehrman's own writings not used in prior formulations.

arguments.weakest_link: The tally of Ehrman citations is asserted from memory without page references, so the hostile-witness point is hard to verify.
arguments.develop_next: Provide exact citations and quotations of Ehrman's '30s' statements.

arguments.name: Majority of scholars date oral tradition to the 30s
arguments.conclusion: A majority of scholars included in Habermas's volume three would place the development of the oral tradition in the 30s AD.
arguments.speaker: Gary Habermas
premises: P1: Habermas has surveyed a large number of scholars in his volumes.
P2: He states that dating the oral tradition to the 30s is very common among them.

st1.quote: Oh, sometime in the 30s I think is very common.

st2.quote: the majority of scholars that you included in in volume three and stuff like that, they they would put this oral tradition developing in that earliest phase

st4.quote: But I think to say the 30s before 40, very common.

st5.quote: Well, anybody can say things that's conservative once in a while.

st6.quote: Oh, sometime in the 30s I think is very common.

st8.quote: I just gave you one for the Jesus Seminar, but a lot of guys who say it from 30 to 39.

arguments.name: Jesus Seminar admits pre-Pauline creed
arguments.conclusion: Even the Jesus Seminar, despite rejecting most of Jesus's words, acknowledges that the 1 Corinthians 15 creed existed before Paul's conversion.
arguments.speaker: Gary Habermas
premises: P1: The Jesus Seminar rejects 91% of the red-letter words of Jesus, and 82% if pink words are included.
P2: In volume two, the Jesus Seminar says that 1 Corinthians 15:3–5 or more verses is a creed Paul cites but did not author.
P3: They say the creed or its component parts existed before Paul's journey to Damascus.
P4: Paul became a Christian two to three years after the cross according to both conservatives and liberals (e.g., Bultmann).
P5: Therefore the creed existed within about two to three years of the crucifixion.

st1.quote: even the Jesus Seminar says before he was converted.

st3.quote: they say in volume two, toward the back, they say that the 1 Corinthians 15:3 and following, three to five or more verses

st4.quote: If he became a Christian two to three years after the cross, that means that at probably plus two, cuz it happened before Paul's two to three.

st5.quote: Well, anybody can say things that's conservative once in a while.

st6.quote: So if they say that and that's plus three max, I would think plus anywhere in the first 10 is pretty

st8.quote: Now, conservatives and liberals believe that Paul became a Christian two to three years, Bultmann, two to three years after the cross.

arguments.prior_art: Robert Funk / Jesus Seminar, The Acts of Jesus (1998), volume two

or1.quote: even the Jesus Seminar says before he was converted
or1.why: Variant hostile-witness use of the Seminar's own creedal admission.

or2.quote: they say in volume two, toward the back, they say that the 1 Corinthians 15:3 and following, three to five or more verses
or2.why: Brings the Seminar's published volume-two statement as new support.

arguments.weakest_link: The move from 'the creed existed before Paul's conversion' to a two-to-three-year window depends on the contested Bultmann chronology.
arguments.develop_next: Cite the exact Jesus Seminar page and the Bultmann reference for the two-to-three-year conversion date.

arguments.name: Paul's persecution implies early creedal knowledge
arguments.conclusion: Paul's pre-conversion persecution of the church makes sense if the early creed was already being taught.
arguments.speaker: Gary Habermas
premises: P1: Paul was 'breathing out threatenings against the church' before his conversion.
P2: He already knew what the early Christians were teaching in the creed.
P3: Romans 10:9, another early creed, contains the classic gospel of deity, death, and resurrection.
P4: If that creed was circulating before Paul's conversion, he would have been angry because it was blasphemy to him.

st1.quote: Cuz he already knew what they were teaching in the early creed.

st2.quote: He said, "Breathing out threatenings against the church."

st3.quote: And verses like Romans 10:9, which is another early creed, "If confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God's raised him from the dead, you'll be saved."

st4.quote: And if that was out there before he was converted, yeah, he's going to be mad because that's blasphemy.

st5.quote: Well, anybody can say things that's conservative once in a while.

st6.quote: Cuz he already knew what they were teaching in the early creed.

st8.quote: And verses like Romans 10:9, which is another early creed

arguments.prior_art: Gary Habermas, pre-Pauline persecution argument in his historical Jesus volumes

or1.quote: Cuz he already knew what they were teaching in the early creed.
or1.why: Variant of the standard persecution/creed inference.

or2.quote: And verses like Romans 10:9, which is another early creed
or2.why: Adds Romans 10:9 as the blasphemy trigger.

arguments.weakest_link: The inference from Paul's persecution to his knowing a specific creed is circumstantial; persecution could target the movement without the formula.
arguments.develop_next: Show an early source linking Paul's persecution directly to the deity/resurrection claim.

arguments.name: Paul's undisputed letters contain early creedal material
arguments.conclusion: The seven undisputed Pauline letters contain early creedal material, and critics grant Paul was an eyewitness.
arguments.speaker: Gary Habermas
premises: P1: Critics admit Paul was an eyewitness and generally accept the seven undisputed letters: Romans, 1–2 Corinthians, Galatians, Philippians, 1 Thessalonians, and Philemon.
P2: Paul has these early verses in those letters.
P3: In Romans 10:9, Paul cites a creed and then applies an Old Testament word for Jehovah to Jesus, indicating deity.
P4: Therefore these creedal statements are very early.

st1.quote: So yeah, these things are very early.

st2.quote: they'll always grant those set first the seven books.

st3.quote: And that's uh Romans, first second Corinthians, Galatians, Philippians, uh first Thessalonians, and the little book Philemon.

st4.quote: In Romans 10:9, it's not his, but the creed he cites, he cites a verse right after it that goes to the Old Testament in the same word in the Greek calls is talking about Jehovah.

st5.quote: Critics admit that Paul was an eyewitness.

st6.quote: I mean, we're talking deity times something here.

st8.quote: In Romans 10:9, it's not his, but the creed he cites, he cites a verse right after it that goes to the Old Testament in the same word in the Greek calls is talking about Jehovah.
